title: Heavier or lighter on a balance scale
examples: How does a balance scale work?

left.label: Watermelon
left.ask: Why does the heavier side go down?

explain.say: Hold a watermelon in one hand and a pineapple in the other. Which is heavier? A balance scale tells you without guessing! Look at the board: the watermelon side goes down, because it is heavier. The pineapple side goes up.

draw.text: Heavier or lighter on a balance scale

left.label: Watermelon
left.ask: Why does the heavier side go down?

explain.say: Let us find out how heavy the watermelon is. Put 4 one-kilogram weights on the other side. Look: the beam is level! Level means both sides have the same mass, so the watermelon is 4 kilograms. Can you see the flat beam?

right.label: Four 1 kg weights
right.ask: What does it mean when the scale is level?

explain.say: Now a surprise. A big fluffy pillow against a small brick. The brick side goes down! The pillow is mostly air, so it is light. Bigger is not always heavier. Can you think of something small but heavy?

A kilogram is a unit for how heavy something is. Here a bag of flour balances one 1 kilogram weight, so the flour is 1 kilogram. Many bags of sugar or flour in shops are 1 kilogram. What else might weigh 1 kilogram?

Well done! Look: a 1 kilogram pineapple and a 3 kilogram bag of rice together balance the 4 kilogram watermelon, because 1 and 3 make 4. Wow: the first balance scales were used in ancient Egypt over 4,000 years ago! What could you weigh at home?

faq.q: Why does the heavier side go down?
faq.a: Gravity pulls harder on the heavier side, so that pan sinks and the lighter pan rises. When both sides are equally heavy, the beam stays level.
asks: How does a balance scale work?

faq.a: No. A big pillow is full of air and feathers, so it is light. A small brick is packed with hard clay, so it is heavy. Only the scale can tell you.
asks: Can a small thing be heavy?

faq.a: A kilogram is a unit for measuring how heavy something is, its mass. A bag of sugar is often 1 kilogram, and a large watermelon can be about 4 kilograms.

faq.q: What does it mean when the scale is level?
faq.a: A level beam means both sides have the same mass. If 4 one-kilogram weights balance a watermelon, the watermelon is 4 kilograms.

faq.q: What is lighter than a kilogram?
faq.a: Small things are measured in grams. There are 1,000 grams in a kilogram, and an apple is about 150 grams.

facts: On a balance scale, the heavier side moves down and the lighter side moves up.
Balance scales were used in ancient Egypt more than 4,000 years ago.

quiz.say: On a balance, the toy car pan goes up and the stone pan goes down. Which is heavier?
quiz.show: On a balance, the toy car pan goes up and the stone pan goes down. Which is heavier?
quiz.why: The heavier side goes down, so the stone is heavier.

wrong.0: The toy car side went up, so it is lighter.
wrong.1: If they weighed the same, the beam would be level.

quiz.say: A watermelon balances 4 one-kilogram weights. How heavy is it?
quiz.show: A watermelon balances 4 one-kilogram weights. How heavy is it?
quiz.why: Level means equal, so the watermelon has the same mass as 4 kilograms.

wrong.1: 1 kilogram is just one of the weights.
wrong.2: 40 kilograms is ten times too heavy.
